audience: Customers, partners, executives, architects, delivery teams, and assurance reviewers

milestones.title: Source-Faithful Local Oracle
milestones.customer_value: Creates a trustworthy local reference for one real CardDemo business process so modernization output can be compared against preserved legacy behavior.
deliverables: A cross-platform Python oracle for the INTCALC batch workload.
Fixed-width CardDemo record parsing and COBOL signed-zoned-decimal support.
Deterministic account and transaction outputs with a hashed evidence receipt.
A candidate comparator that reports exact business-field differences.
A source-faithful policy that preserves the discovered final-account edge case.
boundaries: The oracle is derived from source and is not independent proof of z/OS behavior.
VSAM locking, JES, Language Environment behavior, and EBCDIC collation are not emulated.
Production equivalence requires corroborating authorized legacy execution evidence.

milestones.title: Verified Java and Spring Batch Candidate
milestones.customer_value: Proves that a modern implementation can be built and checked automatically against the source-faithful oracle instead of relying on manual code review.
deliverables: An auditable Java 17, Spring Boot, and Spring Batch modernization candidate.
CardDemo-compatible fixed-width input and output codecs.
COBOL overpunch decoding and encoding in the modern implementation.
Unit, packaging, differential, cross-platform, and CI verification paths.
Separation of batch orchestration from the business transformation.
boundaries: Passing the local oracle proves bounded development equivalence, not z/OS equivalence.
The candidate covers the selected INTCALC slice rather than the full CardDemo estate.
Live operational characteristics remain outside the claim.

milestones.title: Autonomous Factory Run Engine

milestones.title: Verified Semantic Memory

milestones.title: Conflict-Aware Portfolio Factory

milestones.title: CICS, VSAM, IMS, and HLASM Readiness Proofs

milestones.title: Milestone Documentation System
milestones.customer_value: Turns the engineering history into a consistent customer-ready and auditable body of record across Markdown, Word, and PDF.
deliverables: Forty-four canonical milestone narratives covering MS #1 through MS #44.
Matching Markdown, DOCX, and PDF artifacts for every milestone.
A responsive browser index with full-text search across milestone number, title, customer value, capability, boundary, release, and roadmap phase.
Absolute GitHub links for Markdown and PDF plus direct-download links for Microsoft Word, including when the index is viewed outside GitHub.
GitHub Pages publication for the interactive milestone library.
A deterministic generator and content-addressed artifact manifest that also governs the Markdown and HTML indexes.
A fail-closed verifier that detects missing, changed, stale, or extra milestone artifacts.
Roadmap governance that reserves MS #45 for the SAP ASE semantic source adapter.
boundaries: The documents explain and package existing evidence; they do not create new technical qualification or live-system evidence.
Search is performed locally in the browser over the published customer-readable milestone metadata; it is not a search of underlying receipts or customer source code.

milestones.title: SAP ASE Semantic Source Adapter
milestones.customer_value: Lets a customer measure SAP ASE semantic risk before choosing a migration target or accepting a database-conversion claim.
milestones.relationship: Earlier DB2 and Oracle work proved narrower paths. MS #45 qualifies a broader, target-neutral ASE boundary across data, transactions, replication, Transact-SQL, procedures, and triggers before any target claim.
deliverables: A target-neutral SAP ASE SourceAdapter for discovery, privacy-safe profiles, sealed extraction, replication resume, and transaction capabilities.
A 2-table, 31-column catalog with 4 UDTs, 2 identity columns, 5 constraints, 3 indexes, 6 procedures, and 4 triggers.
A 187-case corpus across types, UDTs, identity, money, datetime, strings, Transact-SQL, stored logic, locking, rollback, and replication.
A 107-entry, five-class compatibility ledger covering every catalog object and 54 ASE behaviors.
Twelve gates, five schemas, ten artifacts, cross-platform launchers, and adversarial overclaim tests.
boundaries: Catalog, rows, replication, and transactions are fixtures, not live ASE observations.
Stored logic is inventoried, not natively executed or complete.
No target is selected; PostgreSQL and Oracle qualification remain future pilot work.
Live equivalence, migration completion, and production readiness remain false.

milestones.title: Unified Estate Operator Navigation
milestones.customer_value: Gives an operator one customer-centered graph experience for moving between mainframe and database work while preserving the cross-platform dependencies that explain customer impact.
milestones.relationship: Earlier graph work made individual perspectives explorable, and MS #43/MS #45 qualified Oracle and SAP ASE adapters outside the graph. MS #46 adds an operator model and evidence-aware path tracing across the unified estate without pretending that standalone adapter evidence is already an end-to-end customer integration.
deliverables: A customer, technology-scope, and operator-lens context bar that separates engagement, platform focus, and task perspective.
Unified-estate, mainframe, and database scopes that visually focus the graph without hiding connected cross-platform context; SAP estate and security-vulnerability views are explicitly planned.
Platform classification and coverage metadata for COBOL, PL/I, DB2, VSAM, IMS, JCL, CICS, assembler, BMS, Java, Oracle, SAP ASE, and future SAP evidence.
Directed source-to-target tracing plus a related-evidence mode, platform sequence, hop count, evidence class, and runtime limitation.
First-class IMS DLI statement nodes and ISSUES_DLI, READS_SEGMENT, and WRITES_SEGMENT relationships that resolve source operations through the program's PSB/PCB authorization view.
One-click source-backed COBOL-to-IMS DLET tracing plus a separate non-customer AUTHUPD1 PL/I-to-DB2 UPDATE reference fixture; the original ACCTPL1 path remains a DB2 read.
Visible static-source, static-reference-fixture, non-customer, and runtime-not-observed labels for every proven example.
Search and trace gap states that explain why Oracle and SAP ASE cannot yet participate in an end-to-end graph claim.
Regression tests for directionality, platform coverage, planned lenses, composite PL/I paths, portable UI controls, and documentation integrity.
boundaries: The graph proves committed static and declaration relationships; it does not prove that a production transaction executed.
The COBOL-to-IMS write path proves statically declared DLI mutation intent against an authorized segment; it does not prove that IMS executed or committed the operation.
The AUTHUPD1 PL/I-to-DB2 write is a bundled reference fixture, not customer source; ACCTPL1 remains read-only.
Oracle and SAP ASE qualification artifacts are not yet projected into the graph and have no customer integration call edges.
The bundled customer selector represents the CardDemo reference estate; no customer system is attached.
SAP application and governed security-vulnerability findings remain planned capabilities.
Cross-platform production behavior, live equivalence, and production readiness remain false.

milestones.title: Graph-Bound Live Evidence Control Tower
milestones.customer_value: Gives customers, operators, and executives a credible live command-post view whose status is visibly bound to the same Knowledge Graph identity used by the underlying evidence.
milestones.relationship: MS #17 introduced the live read-only evidence plane, MS #46 added unified-estate navigation and trace, and MS #47 makes the canonical graph itself observable. MS #47.1 through #47.3 close the independent visual, usability, density, local-transport, craft, and accessibility reviews without weakening the evidence boundary.
deliverables: An approved warm editorial product shell using paper-white work surfaces, quiet stone rails, burnt-orange hierarchy, locally served IBM Plex typography, sentence case, rounded controls, and visible interaction states.
A graph-bound Company → Business problem → Workload → Technology scope → Operator lens path with session-stable estate context separated from active work controls.
A dedicated Knowledge Graph binding card showing canonical content identity, entity and relationship counts, freshness, and downstream binding status.
A labelled claim band showing one snapshot identity plus explicit entity, relationship, rule, and validated-extension values.
A 70-node readability guard whose reduction and full-render actions dismiss correctly, with package-collapse, rules-and-proof, and legacy-to-modern choices.
Collision-aware graph labels across five candidate positions, with tooltip preservation and suppression only when no readable placement exists.
Keyboard-operable graph nodes with roving focus, spatial arrow-key navigation, Enter/Space inspection, Home-to-root behavior, descriptive names, and visible focus.
Readable top-control and repeated metadata labels plus a non-clipping accessible live connection status.
A proof-oriented workload action that opens the existing governed proof-run evidence from the inspector.
A first-class graph operational source with hash-chained change events, five-second freshness refresh, and fail-closed downstream identity validation.
Default refusal of non-loopback binds, an explicit exposure override, and a generated per-session bearer token required for verifier-audience HTTP routes.
Locally served SIL-OFL IBM Plex webfonts with no Google Fonts or other runtime asset request.
Regression coverage across policy, HTTP authorization, UI contracts, graph binding, density behavior, label placement, freshness, and documentation.
boundaries: The Control Tower remains a read-only projection and does not gain approve, dispatch, retry, promote, or exception-authoring authority.
Implementer routes remain unauthenticated and are safe only on loopback; the explicit non-loopback override does not make a deployment secure.
The verifier token is per-session audience authorization, not enterprise identity, RBAC, or a substitute for customer SSO/OIDC at a reverse proxy.
Graph freshness proves observation of the committed snapshot and evidence pack; it does not prove customer runtime behavior.
A graph change invalidates mismatched downstream evidence; it does not automatically regenerate or approve that evidence.
Customer execution evidence, native platform equivalence, and production readiness remain false.

milestones.title: iDempiere Oracle Reference Estate Inventory
milestones.customer_value: Replaces a toy Oracle source with a pinned, enterprise-shaped ERP reference estate while measuring its size and preserving the boundary between static inventory and behavioral proof.
milestones.relationship: MS #43 qualified a bounded Oracle source adapter and MS #47 made evidence graph identity operational. MS #48 selects and measures the larger Oracle-equivalent reference estate that will supply future source and graph coverage without importing it into product runtime or upgrading static evidence into equivalence.
deliverables: A supported iDempiere release-13 pin at commit 731515dcdd5278b843db33b9d3109d155b881951 with source, tree, date, and GPL-2.0 license identity.
A reproducible inventory tool that refuses a dirty checkout or any commit other than the pin and emits only derived counts and source-path references.
A measured 12,565-file estate with a 4,520-node, 36,819-edge internal Java source-unit graph and 2,823 Oracle SQL files.
An order-to-cash slice with 12 seed source units and a one-hop graph of 181 nodes and 497 edges.
A procure-to-pay slice with 12 seed source units and a one-hop graph of 177 nodes and 475 edges.
Curated document-flow maps that preserve the shared physical tables and the IsSOTrx and IsReceipt business selectors.

Eight prioritized Oracle semantic fixtures covering empty-string/null, NUMBER precision and scale, DATE arithmetic, NVL/DECODE coercion, ROWNUM ordering, SELECT FOR UPDATE, NO_DATA_FOUND, and LOB boundaries.
Regression checks for pin identity, graph measurements, slice semantics, corpus posture, non-vendoring, and explicit claim boundaries.
boundaries: The iDempiere source is not vendored, built, executed, translated, or attached to product runtime.
The measured graph is a static Java source-unit dependency graph, not a complete application-dictionary, runtime, transaction, or database-foreign-key graph.
The two mapped slices are upstream reference flows, not customer source or observed customer transactions.
Oracle's official sample schemas are identified as the dialect authority but are not acquired or executed in this milestone.
CloudBank remains the intended modern destination, but no iDempiere-to-CloudBank mapping is claimed.
Native Oracle behavior, application equivalence, migration completion, and production readiness remain false.

milestones.title: Oracle Dialect Authority Corpus and Executable Fixtures
milestones.customer_value: Replaces Oracle-semantics assumptions with a pinned official source corpus and executable cases while keeping native-database proof visibly separate.

MS #49 acquires the official Oracle dialect authority, executes a deterministic local semantics model, and emits a native Oracle harness without promoting either activity into iDempiere application equivalence.
deliverables: An Oracle Database Sample Schemas v23.3 pin at commit e3325a83e56c516815844025418a96ecaf219751 with exact tree and MIT license identities.
An allowlisted nine-file corpus spanning customer_orders, human_resources, and sales_history: four SQL files, 2,000 SQL lines, and 77,919 bytes.

Eight executable fixtures and 24 deterministic cases covering empty-string/null, NUMBER precision and scale, DATE arithmetic, NVL/DECODE coercion, ROWNUM ordering, SELECT FOR UPDATE, SELECT INTO/NO_DATA_FOUND, and LOB boundaries.
A content-addressed model-conformance receipt recording all 24 cases as passed-bounded-model while native execution and equivalence flags remain false.
A fail-fast native Oracle SQL harness with one completion marker for each fixture and no simulated native result.
CLI, POSIX shell, and PowerShell build and verification paths for acquisition, generated artifacts, hashes, schemas, results, and claim boundaries.
JSON schemas plus adversarial tests that reject altered content, rehashed native-execution overclaims, and application-equivalence overclaims.
boundaries: The selected corpus is a deliberately bounded official-source subset, not the complete sample-schema repository or its bulk data.
The deterministic local semantics model does not constitute native Oracle execution or conformance.
The native SQL harness is generated but unexecuted; no authorized database identity, session, transaction, lock, or LOB runtime evidence is claimed.
No iDempiere application behavior or customer transaction is executed or proven equivalent.
No iDempiere-to-CloudBank mapping is complete.
Native Oracle conformance, application equivalence, migration completion, and production readiness remain false.

milestones.title: Oracle Semantic Coverage Program
milestones.customer_value: Gives database architects a quantified, evidence-levelled Oracle coverage answer and completes bounded catalog execution across core SQL, datatypes, PL/SQL, transactions, operations, schema/DML, schema objects, and structured data.
milestones.relationship: MS #49 proved the mechanism with eight fixtures and 24 cases. MS #50.0 made them bootstrap evidence inside a governed broad-coverage program; MS #50.1 executes 920 core SQL/type cases, MS #50.2 executes 320 PL/SQL cases, MS #50.3 executes 280 transaction and operations cases, and MS #50.4 executes the final 480 schema/DML, schema-object, and structured-data cases without promoting bounded-model evidence into native Oracle proof.
deliverables: A catalog of 500 stable Oracle behavior contracts and 2,000 case specifications across ten exact domains.
Bounded execution of 920 governed core SQL/type cases, 320 PL/SQL cases, 280 transaction and operations cases, and 480 schema/DML, schema-object, and structured-data cases.

Schema and structured-data coverage spanning DML state changes, defaults, identity, constraints, indexes, schema evolution, views, sequences, synonyms, partitioning, materialized views, index-organized tables, editions, BLOB, CLOB, SecureFiles, JSON, XMLType, and object types.
Separately declared expectations and independently computed observations across 100 topic families, five behavior focuses, and four case dimensions.

A deduplicated evidence ladder reporting 500 catalogued, 500 catalog-executed, 500 unique bounded-model verified, 0 native-verified, and 0 target-equivalent behaviors, with 2,024 evidence records after retaining the 24 bootstrap runs separately.
Native execution plans plus deterministic artifacts, ten JSON Schemas, cross-platform verification, and adversarial dependency-drift, mutation, overlap, and overclaim tests.
boundaries: The 2,000 passed catalog cases are deterministic bounded-model evidence; they do not constitute native Oracle execution or conformance.
No governed catalog cases remain unexecuted, but native Oracle verified and target-equivalent behavior counts remain zero.
The 24 MS #49 bootstrap runs remain separate evidence records and all eight behavior bindings overlap executed catalog tranches.

Physical storage and index behavior, partitioning, materialized-view refresh, edition visibility, SecureFiles and LOB locator semantics, native JSON/XML/object behavior, and the 19c-to-26ai JSON datatype delta remain bounded until authorized native evidence exists.
No native Oracle 19c or 26ai execution receipt exists.
Catalogued is not supported; bounded-model verified is not native conformant; native verified is not target equivalent.
iDempiere projection, CloudBank mapping, application equivalence, migration completion, and production readiness remain false.

milestones.title: Oracle Native Execution Admission Gate
milestones.customer_value: Defines the admissible evidence required before an Oracle 19c or 26ai conformance claim can be accepted.
milestones.relationship: MS #50 completed 2,000 bounded cases with native counts at zero. MS #51 maps them to 19c and 26ai and defines the signed gate for future native runs.
deliverables: A content-addressed manifest mapping all 500 behaviors and 2,000 catalog cases to both 19c and 26ai, defining 4,000 required native executions.
A 20-batch version/domain run-pack index with exact case counts and visible harness-materialization and execution states.
A native execution contract binding database and session identity, expectation, harness and observation hashes, diagnostics, timestamps, runner identity, and runtime-key signatures.
External-wallet-only authentication and a no-credential, no-raw-output repository policy.
A strict receipt verifier rejecting unsigned evidence, unknown or duplicate cases, version or binding drift, unsafe security posture, partial promotion, and overclaims.
Three JSON Schemas, deterministic artifacts, cross-platform CLI verification, and adversarial admission tests.
boundaries: Release 0.51.0 materializes zero of 4,000 SQL harnesses and executes zero cases on an authorized Oracle database.
The MS #49 eight-fixture SQL file lacks per-case native observations and is ineligible as catalog-native evidence.
A signed partial receipt proves only its cases; it cannot promote a database lane to conformance.
A lane becomes conformant only after all 2,000 cases pass against one bound database identity and the exact SQL harnesses.
Native Oracle conformance does not establish target equivalence.
No credentials, wallets, verification keys, or raw SQL output are committed.
iDempiere equivalence, CloudBank mapping, migration completion, and production readiness remain false.

milestones.title: Oracle Customer (Large) Control Tower Projection
milestones.customer_value: Lets operators explore a large Oracle reference estate through business-facing order-to-cash and procure-to-pay workloads without presenting public reference evidence as an attached customer system.
milestones.relationship: MS #48 pinned and measured the upstream reference estate, MS #50 broadened Oracle semantic coverage, and MS #51 defined native execution admission. MS #52 now projects the two curated business slices into the Control Tower under the operator-facing name Oracle Customer (Large) while preserving the earlier evidence boundaries.

Order-to-cash and procure-to-pay business problems and workloads bound to the two curated nine-table reference slices.
Twenty static document-flow trace scenarios covering order, shipment or receipt, invoice, payment, and allocation relationships.
A deterministic content-addressed graph fragment and receipt bound to the exact canonical graph, source commit, tree, inventory, selectors, and slice evidence.
Composition with the existing PL/I extension while retaining the canonical CardDemo graph as the runtime and audit identity.
POSIX and Windows build and verification launchers plus adversarial naming, drift, provenance, platform, and overclaim tests.
boundaries: Oracle Customer (Large) is an operator-facing public reference-estate label; no customer system is attached.
iDempiere remains only as upstream source, commit, tree, license, and internal evidence provenance.
The 20 projected relationships are curated static trace scenarios, not native Oracle execution or observed transactions.
The projection does not change the canonical CardDemo graph or promote its runtime and audit claims.
Native Oracle conformance, application equivalence, CloudBank mapping, migration completion, and production readiness remain false.

milestones.title: CloudBank Modern Oracle Reference Estate

MS #53 adds a deliberately different source: Oracle's modern Java and Kubernetes CloudBank v5 application, proving the factory story covers database decoupling in contemporary microservices as well as visibly legacy estates.
deliverables: An exact pin of Oracle's official CloudBank v5 reference application at commit 4f41b16d00c45503f691836fee8138010c969e86 with tree and UPL-1.0 license identities.
A reproducible static inventory of 189 files, 70 Java source units, ten Maven modules, ten deployable units, nine SQL files, and 62 Spring/JAX-RS endpoint annotations.
A selectable CloudBank Reference Estate company context alongside CardDemo and Oracle Customer (Large).
Five business workloads covering customer/accounts, money transfer, cheque processing, identity/authorization, and credit scoring.
Twenty curated migration-risk scenarios spanning Oracle schema semantics, LRA compensation, transactional messaging, security, audit triggers, nondeterminism, and operations.
Explicit PostgreSQL, PostgreSQL-compatible distributed SQL, and other adapter-qualified relational candidate lanes with no prematurely selected target.
A deterministic content-addressed graph fragment and receipt composed with the existing PL/I and Oracle Customer (Large) fragments.
Cross-platform launchers, release documentation, deterministic checks, and adversarial target-overclaim rejection.
boundaries: The upstream CloudBank source is not vendored, built, or executed.
The inventory and migration-risk projection are static source evidence, not runtime observations.
CloudBank Reference Estate is a public reference estate, not an attached customer system.
Candidate target lanes are options rather than a target selection or database mapping.
No schema conversion, generated application refactoring, dual-run comparison, or native target execution is complete.
PostgreSQL compatibility, target equivalence, application equivalence, migration completion, and production readiness remain false.

milestones.customer_value: Turns the pinned CloudBank estate into a reproducible, fail-closed source execution contract so the first dark factory workcell can start from proven Oracle behavior instead of static inventory alone.

deliverables: A deterministic Java 21 and Maven 3.6-or-newer build plan bound to the exact 189-file, 70-Java-unit, ten-module CloudBank v5 source tree.
A reproducible build of the seven-service set declared by the pinned upstream image-build script, with seven JAR hashes required in the signed receipt.

Content-addressed readiness, build, and Oracle-runtime contracts plus three JSON Schemas.
Environment-key-signed receipts that retain aggregate results and hashes while excluding credentials, raw stdout, and raw stderr.
Strict verification rejecting unsigned evidence, source or plan drift, Java 17, old Maven, missing artifacts, failed or skipped tests, image-identity gaps, and PostgreSQL or production overclaims.
Cross-platform launchers and a Java 21 CI source-build job that exercises the exact pinned upstream checkout.
An explicit data boundary: pinned sample and bootstrap data qualify the first controlled run, while production data requires a separately authorized and profiled extract.
boundaries: The committed readiness receipt says ready-to-execute-not-observed because this development environment has not produced an authorized Java 21, Docker, and Oracle execution receipt.
The bounded Oracle runtime suite proves only the azn-server source baseline; it does not execute the customer service or the complete CloudBank application.
The upstream source is required as an exact external checkout and is not vendored into this repository.
No customer or production CloudBank data is present, copied, or implied.
PostgreSQL target selection and mapping do not begin until the source runtime receipt is admitted.
PostgreSQL compatibility, target equivalence, application equivalence, migration completion, and production readiness remain false.

deliverables: A source contract binding the pinned customer DDL, bootstrap data, JPA code, Oracle configuration, and Maven module.
A seven-column, primary-key mapping from CUSTOMER.CUSTOMERS to cloudbank_customer.customers on PostgreSQL 16.
Explicit handling of Oracle empty strings, identifier folding, DATE/SYSDATE precision, UTC policy, and C-collation fragment searches.
A compatibility ledger exposing the ROLE/JPA mismatch, Oracle UCP/wallet refactor, API authorization boundary, and production policies.
Synthetic four-row fixtures containing neither upstream demonstration passwords nor production data.
A hardened postgres:16-alpine runner checking the catalog, defaults, normalization, searches, CRUD, commit, and rollback.
